lines.trans: Reporter Kang, you came here again?
A PD should be at the station, yet you're always at the Commission.
Please stop writing articles bashing our show.
Once it's gone, I won't even be able to bash it.
What are you talking about?
I heard it's getting cancelled.
Usually the production crew is the very last to know about a cancellation.
Why wouldn't I know about my own show?

meanings.note: 기자 + honorific suffix -님, used when addressing a reporter respectfully

examples.trans: Reporter, may I ask just one question?

examples.text: 강 기자님은 오늘도 현장에 나와 있습니다.
examples.trans: Reporter Kang is out on the scene again today.

meanings.note: indicates repetition of an action or event
adds another item or point

examples.trans: Let's meet again tomorrow.
It started raining again.

meanings.note: movement toward the speaker or reference point
used with weather phenomena like 비가 오다

examples.trans: When did you come to Korea?
My friend came over to my house.

meanings.note: from English 'PD'; refers to a television or radio producer-director in Korea

examples.trans: He is a famous variety show PD.
The PD said to start filming.

meanings.note: 방송 (broadcasting) + 국 (bureau/station)

examples.trans: I have to go to the TV station this afternoon.
Fans are waiting in front of the broadcasting station.

있다.gloss: to be (in a place), to exist, to have

meanings.note: used with locative -에 to express where someone or something is
expresses existence or possession

examples.trans: I am in the office right now.
Do you have time tomorrow?

related.gloss: to not be, to not have

meanings.en: always, all the time, every day
meanings.note: colloquial pronunciation/variant of 만날; often carries mild exasperation

examples.trans: He always comes late.
Why do you make the same mistake every time?

meanings.note: abbreviation of 방송통신위원회, South Korea's broadcasting and telecommunications regulator

examples.trans: A Broadcast Commission meeting was held today.
The Broadcast Commission announced new regulations.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun
used before nouns to show collective or personal belonging (e.g., 우리 집, 우리 프로그램)

examples.trans: Shall we eat lunch together?
Our team won first place this time.

meanings.note: spoken contraction of bound noun 것; refers to an object, matter, or show

examples.trans: Whose is this?
Let's go eat something delicious.

까다.gloss: to bash, roast, criticize harshly; to peel

meanings.note: slang usage in media and everyday speech meaning to criticize harshly
literal meaning, as in peeling fruit or eggs

examples.text: 인터넷에서 그 영화를 너무 심하게 까더라.
examples.trans: People on the internet were bashing that movie so hard.
I peeled a tangerine and ate it.

meanings.note: written piece in a newspaper or online media

examples.trans: I read that article this morning.

examples.text: 새 드라마에 대한 기사가 많이 나왔어요.
examples.trans: Many articles came out about the new drama.

meanings.note: softens requests, commands, or complaints in spoken Korean
contraction of 조금

examples.trans: Please close the door.
I have a bit much work lately.

meanings.note: used before a verb to tell someone to stop an ongoing action

examples.trans: Stop worrying now.
I'm so full I'll stop eating.

meanings.note: writing text, articles, letters, etc.
using a tool, time, or money

examples.trans: I write a diary every day.
Please write your name here.

없어지다.gloss: to disappear, vanish; to be cancelled

meanings.note: something ceases to exist or be present
used for shows, programs, or policies being discontinued

examples.trans: The key that was on the desk disappeared.
That program was cancelled last year.

meanings.note: auxiliary verb following -지 to express inability or impossibility
used as a main verb after a noun (e.g., 요리를 못하다)

examples.trans: I was busy so I couldn't eat lunch.
I couldn't sleep well yesterday.

meanings.note: spoken contraction of 무슨, placed before a noun

examples.trans: What are you thinking about so deeply right now?
What's going on all of a sudden?

meanings.note: in expressions like 뭔 소리야? ('what are you talking about?')
audible sound made by people or things

examples.trans: Suddenly a strange sound was heard.

examples.text: 말도 안 되는 소리 하지 마.
examples.trans: Don't talk nonsense.

meanings.note: describes how things typically work
refers to an initial state or plan

examples.trans: Traffic is usually heavy on Mondays.
This place was originally a park.

meanings.note: loanword from English 'program'
software or planned sequence of events

examples.trans: There are many fun variety shows these days.
I am planning a new show.

meanings.en: cancellation (of a show), abolition (of a system or law)
meanings.note: official discontinuation of a program, rule, or institution

examples.trans: The show's cancellation was decided due to low ratings.
That system was abolished last year.

meanings.note: 제작 (production) + 진 (group/staff); the PDs, writers, and crew making a show

examples.trans: The production crew prepared the shoot all night.
Both the production crew and the cast worked hard.

meanings.note: superlative adverb placed before an adjective or adverb

examples.text: 한국 음식 중에서 비빔밥을 제일 좋아해요.
examples.trans: Among Korean foods, I like bibimbap the most.
Today is the coldest day of this week.

meanings.note: takes -게 to form the adverb 늦게 ('late')

examples.trans: Traffic was backed up, so I was late to my appointment.
I went to sleep too late last night.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb (stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ)
e.g., 알겠어요 ('I understand')

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I understand what you mean.

meanings.note: casual/plain possessive determiner (contraction of 나의); polite equivalent is 제

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Listen to what I'm saying.

meanings.note: casual/plain 1st person singular pronoun; becomes 내가 before subject particle -가

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: interrogative adverb

examples.trans: Why are you so tired today?
Why didn't you answer the phone?

meanings.en: to not know, be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb (stem 모르- becomes 몰라요 in polite present)

examples.trans: I didn't know that fact either.
If there is a word you don't know, look it up.

meanings.note: used with -에 as 다음에 ('next time')

examples.trans: Let's drink coffee together next time.
We have to get off at the next station.

meanings.note: used in farewells like 다음에 또 봐요 ('see you next time')
watching TV, movies, or reading

examples.trans: I decided to meet my friend on the weekend.
I watched an interesting movie yesterday.
